subtopic: Allocating Among Stocks, Bonds, and Cash
source_evidence: The allocation that works best for you changes at different times in your life, depending on your investing timeframe or time horizon and your risk tolerance.
answer: Asset allocation means dividing your investments among assets such as stocks, bonds, and cash. The mix that may fit you depends in part on how long you plan to invest and your willingness and ability to risk losing some or all of your original investment. People with longer time horizons may feel comfortable with riskier or more volatile investments, while those with shorter horizons may prefer less risky or less volatile investments. Diversification means spreading money among different investments to reduce risk; allocating across different asset classes is one way to diversify. The source does not prescribe a single mix for everyone.
